heading: Generic errors
text:
## Generic errors [NERR.4]

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `DS_ERR_INVAL`       | NULL pointer to a non-optional argument; invalid enum; out-of-range integer |
| `DS_ERR_OOM`         | allocation failed inside libds; its detail may be NULL ([NERR.2.3]) |
| `DS_ERR_NOT_FOUND`   | required lookup miss (e.g. `ds_engine_schema_at` out of range) |
| `DS_ERR_STATE`       | rejected by current engine state (e.g. `ds_engine_clock_set` in live mode; **any** call from inside a callback into the engine that invoked it, a pump's or an enumerating read's, [RARC.13.16], [RARC.13.17]; a second `ds_engine_load_dsc` on one engine, [NFCT.1.1]) |
| `DS_ERR_OVERFLOW`    | a bounded queue / counter would overflow (internal boundaries) |
| `DS_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` | an operation unavailable in this build (e.g. `ds_engine_mem` is RETE-only) |
| `DS_ERR_INTERNAL`    | invariant violation inside libds — a bug; file an issue with the detail |
| `DS_ERR_IO`          | an integrator callback (a recording sink, a storage backend, [NSTG.3.3]) reports a failure of its own I/O. libds performs no I/O and raises it nowhere itself; the call whose callback returned it returns it ([NCBK.1.5]) |
| `DS_ERR_ENGINE_HALTED` | an `EngineError` halted the tier, or a load failed ([RDSC.9.8]). Returned by the call that raised the `EngineError`, and by every later call but the few [NCBK.2.9] leaves valid, which does nothing; a failed load returns its own code. Returned whatever caused the halt — the cause is carried by the `EngineError` or the failed load's status, not by this code ([NCBK.2.9]) |
